cues.en: Of course I want to try to retrieve data whenever the app restarts and therefore, I'll add a new method
autoLogin, you can name it whatever you want and
this is a method that simply tries to fetch data from the storage and if it finds data that is valid,
it actually logs us in. For that, I'll access plugin storage or plugins, excuse me, storage get and now
get takes an object where we define the key for which we want to get our data and that is the key I defined
when I stored data,
so that's auth data in this case here,
so up there in autoLogin, auth data is the key which I want to search for in my storage and
now this returns a promise.
Now we could work with a promise here but I actually want to turn this into an observable and hence,
I will return an observable here by using the from creation operator which you simply import from rxjs.
So you import from here and from takes for example a promise and it automatically manages the
listening to that promise response so to say and converts it into an observable.
Now of course, I don't just want to return the raw data, I want to return the information whether this
succeeded or not,
so I want to return true or false here because later we can then for example use that in the auth guard
but more on that in a second. Hence, it's time to add the pipe method here and execute a couple of steps
and I will need the map operator to convert that data I'm extracting from the storage to something I
can use for actually creating a user object. So we get our stored data here and that stored data could
of course not be set
if we never stored data before. So if we don't have stored data or if this stored data does not have
a value field which it normally should have, then I will return null here, then I was not able to extract
any useful data, otherwise we can continue
and the fact that we have a value field on the stored data simply stems from the storage plugin giving
us such a value field on the data it returns from the storage.
So here, I will then get my parsed data, you can name this however you want of course by using JSON parse
to convert that stored string back into a Javascript object by using store, by passing stored data value
in there and this will actually give us an object that has a token and I do this with the as operator
here to tell Typescript which kind of data is returned by this. So we'll have a token which is a string,
we'll have, let's have a look,
what did I name it? We'll have a token expiration date,
so we'll have the fields I stored down there, we'll have a token expiration date which is also a string,
not a date object,
it was converted to a string before in our store auth data method and we'll have our userId,
which is a string. So exactly that data you did store down there though the order of the properties does
not matter. So that is the data we get back by parsing the stored data.
Now I need to convert my expiration time into a date object and for that, we can simply create a new
date object and pass in the parsed data token expiration date field value because that is a string
that actually has the ISO format that can be used by the date constructor.
Now of course, that is a date now but it might already be an expired token.
So if the expiration time is smaller or equal than the current time, then this means it is in the past
and therefore that token expired,
so then I will also return null because I was able to retrieve data but it will not be useful data.
If we make it past this if check, then we can actually create a new user,
so I'll create a new user and there, I need to store my ID, e-mail and so on.
Well since I need that e-mail, actually I should store that e-mail in my storage as well,
so in store auth data, I'll store the e-mail now and I expect to get the e-mail here as a string,
so let's store e-mail. Since I expect it as a string here, we need to pass it here
when we call store auth date of course, there I want to pass in my e-mail and now when we extract our
data up there,
well that parsed data of course now will have an e-mail field as well because we're now storing this as
well.
Now we can create our new user here and that user gets the ID from parsed data userId, the e-mail from
parsed data e-mail, of course also the token from parsed data token and for the expiration time, it's our expiration
time object, date object we're creating up there.
This is now the user we're creating
and now, I will return my user here.
So we either return null if we have invalid data or we were not able to retrieve data or we return a user
object.
Now this is just in this map
operator I added to pipe,
it's not the only operator I want to have in this chain though.
I'll also add a tap
operator where I get this user object now
and of course only if the user is set, I will then emit this user.
So in my private user property, I will call next and forward this user because I want to emit that user
in case I have it.
And last but not least, this observable chain should not return a user object but true or false,
so I'll add another map
operator where I also get that user because tap never consumes the data, just taps in but doesn't
change it.
So I get a user object here and I want to return a boolean, so I'll use that double exclamation mark
trick to force that into a boolean
and now we return true if we have a user or if we returned null before,
well we return false here.
This is the autoLogin method,
now where do I want to use that?
